title: [Files] FileDownloader deletes partial/complete download on any non-206 response
body:
## Summary
When resuming, `FileDownloader` deletes the existing file for any status other than 206 — including 5xx/4xx error responses — before checking whether the response is successful.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:163` — `if (existingSize > 0 && response.StatusCode != HttpStatusCode.PartialContent)` deletes `destinationPath` and resets `existingSize`
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs` — `ThrowIfNotSuccessful` only runs after this block

## Problem
With `EnableResume` (default), a resume attempt that gets 503, 404, 401 or a captive-portal 200 wipes the partial file. A 5xx while re-downloading to a path that already holds a complete file also deletes the complete file. Transient server errors therefore cause data loss and force full re-downloads on mobile.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §15.3.7 (206 Partial Content), §14.2 (Range)

## Suggested fix
1. Check `IsSuccessStatusCode` (and 416) first; on error throw without touching the file.
2. Only discard the partial file on a successful 200 (server ignored Range) or after a 416.
3. Download into `<path>.part` and atomically rename on success so the final path never holds a truncated or deleted file (see also the resume-safety issue).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Non-success responses on a resume attempt leave the existing partial/complete file untouched
- [ ] 200 on a resume attempt restarts from scratch (expected)
- [ ] Regression test: partial file + server 503 -> file still present with original length

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Cache] Cache stores 206 partial responses and ignores Range/If-Range
body:
## Summary
`CacheInterceptor` treats any 2xx as storable, including 206, and does not look at `Range`/`If-Range`/`Content-Range` on lookup or store.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:768` — `ShouldConsiderForStorage` accepts 200–299
- No `Range`/`Content-Range` handling anywhere in the Cache assembly

## Problem
`FileDownloader` sends `Range: bytes=N-`. A 206 with `Cache-Control: max-age` is stored as the full representation for that URL; a later plain GET is served the partial body with status 206. Conversely, a Range GET is answered from a cached full 200, so the downloader appends the whole file to its partial file.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 §3 and §3.3 (storing incomplete responses), RFC 9110 §14 (Range requests)

## Suggested fix
1. Only store final responses whose status is cacheable by default (RFC 9111 §3 / RFC 9110 §15.1: 200, 203, 204, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, 501) or explicitly allowed; never store 206 unless partial-content storage is implemented per RFC 9111 §3.3.
2. Bypass the cache (no lookup, no store) when the request carries `Range` or `If-Range`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 206 responses are never stored
- [ ] Requests with `Range`/`If-Range` bypass cache lookup
- [ ] Regression tests for both directions (partial stored as full; Range answered from full)

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Cache] Unsafe-method invalidation and revalidation force full buffering and break streaming
body:
## Summary
Cache invalidation (POST/PUT/DELETE) and revalidation paths collect the full response in memory and flip the shared streaming flag, defeating Phase 22a streaming whenever `CacheInterceptor` is in the pipeline.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:348` — `HandleUnsafeInvalidationAsync` uses `TransportDispatchHelper.CollectResponseAsync`
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:377` — `RevalidateAsync` same
- `BufferedDispatchBridge` sets `context.SetState(StreamingResponseRequested, false)` on the shared context and never restores it; `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Stream.cs:109` reads the flag live
- `ReplayCollectedResponseAsync` copies again via `ToArray`

## Problem
A streamed POST (SSE, LLM chat streaming) becomes fully buffered as soon as `CacheInterceptor` is configured. A GET with a stale entry (e.g. a large download) is buffered entirely in memory, then copied — OOM risk on mobile.

## Suggested fix
1. Unsafe methods: pass the response straight through and perform invalidation in a handler wrapper on response start (status 2xx/3xx) without buffering.
2. Revalidation: stream the response; only buffer when status is 304 (empty body) and merge; for 200 tee into the store using the existing streaming accumulator.
3. Never mutate `StreamingResponseRequested` on the caller's context (or restore it in `finally`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Streaming POST through `CacheInterceptor` is delivered incrementally (first chunk before body completes)
- [ ] Revalidation returning 200 with a large body does not allocate the full body before the consumer reads
- [ ] `StreamingResponseRequested` is unchanged after a cache dispatch
- [ ] Allocation-gate test covering both paths

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Auth] OAuth refresh drops the refresh token when the server does not rotate it
body:
## Summary
`OAuthClient.RefreshTokenAsync` stores a token parsed only from the refresh response; if the response omits `refresh_token`, the stored refresh token becomes null.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:200-201` — `ParseTokenResponse(...)` then `_tokenStore.SetAsync(key, token, ct)`

## Problem
Most providers do not rotate refresh tokens. After the first refresh the store holds a token with `RefreshToken == null`; when the access token expires again `GetValidTokenAsync` cannot refresh and returns the expired token, so every request gets 401 until the user re-authenticates.

## Spec reference
RFC 6749 §6 (refresh token MAY be issued; client keeps the old one otherwise)

## Suggested fix
When the token response has no `refresh_token`, carry over the refresh token used for the request (`request.RefreshToken`) into the new `OAuthToken` before storing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Refresh response without `refresh_token` keeps the previous refresh token
- [ ] Refresh response with a new `refresh_token` replaces it
- [ ] Regression test: two consecutive expirations both refresh successfully

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Retry] Retry-After is not capped by MaxDelay and can stall a call indefinitely
body:
## Summary
A server-provided `Retry-After` overrides the computed backoff whenever it is larger, with no upper bound.

## Location
- `Runtime/Retry/RetryPolicy.cs:156-161` — `minimumDelayOverride` wins over the `MaxDelay`-capped delay
- `RetryInterceptor` awaits `Task.Delay(delay, ct)`; request `Timeout` is per attempt and does not bound the wait

## Problem
`Retry-After: 86400` on a 503/429 stalls the call for a day (or until the caller cancels). A misconfigured or hostile server can pin client requests and their concurrency permits.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §10.2.3 (Retry-After)

## Suggested fix
1. Clamp the override to `MaxDelay` or a new `MaxRetryAfter` (default e.g. 60 s).
2. If `Retry-After` exceeds the cap, fail fast (return the last response) instead of waiting.
3. Consider an overall retry budget (total elapsed) on `RetryPolicy`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Retry-After greater than the cap never produces a delay above the cap (or returns immediately per policy)
- [ ] Unit test with `Retry-After: 86400` completes within the cap
- [ ] Docs describe the behavior

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Core] Add pipeline ordering model / construction-time validation for interceptors
body:
## Summary
Interceptor order determines correctness and security, but it is only 'order added' with no documentation of a safe order and no enforcement.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/Pipeline/InterceptorPipeline.cs` — chain built in list order
- `Documentation~/Modules/Middleware.md` — only says 'order they are added' and refers to non-existent `UHttpClientOptions.Middlewares`

## Problem
Concrete failure modes:
- Redirect outer + Auth inner: bearer token re-added on cross-origin hop (separate security issue).
- Cache outer + Auth inner: cache never sees `Authorization`, bypassing `AllowCacheForAuthorizedRequests=false`; per-user `private` responses cached under a user-less key and served after an account switch.
- Cookie outer + Redirect inner: Set-Cookie of redirect hops lost / stored under the wrong host (separate issue).
- Concurrency outer + Retry inner: permit held during backoff sleeps up to `MaxDelay`.

## Suggested fix
1. Give first-party interceptors an `Order`/phase (e.g. Observability → Redirect → Cookie → Auth → Cache → Retry → Decompression → Concurrency) and sort, or
2. Validate at `UHttpClient` construction and throw/warn on known-bad combinations.
3. Document the canonical order and the reason for each constraint.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Known-bad orderings are rejected or auto-corrected with a logged warning
- [ ] Documented canonical order
- [ ] Tests for each failure mode listed above

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Auth] AuthInterceptor re-adds Authorization after cross-origin redirect
body:
## Summary
`RedirectInterceptor` strips `Authorization` on cross-origin hops, but when `AuthInterceptor` sits inside it, Auth unconditionally sets the header again on the redirected request, leaking the bearer token to the third-party host.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:32` — `WithHeader("Authorization", ...)` for every request
- `Runtime/Middleware/RedirectInterceptor.cs` — `BuildRedirectRequest` strips credentials on origin change

## Problem
API at `api.example.com` replies `302 Location: https://cdn.thirdparty.net/file`. With pipeline [Redirect, Auth], the redirected request passes through Auth again and carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to `cdn.thirdparty.net`.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §15.4 (redirection; user agents should not forward credentials cross-origin)

## Suggested fix
1. Bind auth to an origin: `AuthInterceptor` takes an allowed origin set (default: origin of the first request / configured base URI) and only injects for matching scheme+host+port.
2. Have RedirectInterceptor mark derived cross-origin requests (metadata flag) and have Auth respect it.
3. Never inject over plain http unless explicitly allowed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Cross-origin redirect never carries the token regardless of interceptor order
- [ ] Same-origin redirect keeps auth
- [ ] Regression test for both orders [Redirect, Auth] and [Auth, Redirect]

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Middleware] Decompression fails on HEAD/204/304 responses that carry Content-Encoding
body:
## Summary
`DecompressionHandler` tries to decode empty bodies of bodiless responses and throws 'GZIP payload is truncated'.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:~75` and `:180` — no status/method check before decoding

## Problem
A HEAD request to a gzip-served resource, or a 304 that repeats `Content-Encoding: gzip`, fails with `OnResponseError("Response decompression failed")` instead of returning headers. Breaks cache revalidation (304) for compressed resources when Decompression is in the chain.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §9.3.2 (HEAD), §15.4.5 (304), §8.4 (Content-Encoding)

## Suggested fix
Skip decompression when the request method is HEAD, the status is 1xx/204/304, or the body length is 0.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HEAD and 304 with `Content-Encoding: gzip` succeed and keep headers intact
- [ ] Regression tests for HEAD, 204, 304

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Cookies] Cookies from redirect hops are stored under the original host
body:
## Summary
`CookieInterceptor` pins the first request's URI in its handler, so cookies from later hops are attributed to the wrong host.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieInterceptor.cs:69` — `new CookieHandler(handler, _jar, requestForNext.Uri)`

## Problem
With Cookie outer and Redirect inner, 3xx responses are consumed by RedirectHandler and their Set-Cookie never reaches the jar; the final response from host B is stored against host A. A host-only cookie from B is then sent to A — cross-host cookie injection/leak.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 §5.3 (storage model, request-uri), §5.4

## Suggested fix
1. Resolve the cookie origin per hop from the request in `OnRequestStart(request)` / the response's request URI.
2. Ensure redirect hops pass Set-Cookie through the jar (cookie handling inside each hop), or enforce Redirect-outer ordering via the ordering model.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Set-Cookie on each redirect hop is stored for that hop's host
- [ ] Final-hop cookies are stored for the final host
- [ ] Regression test with A -> 302 -> B both setting host-only cookies

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Cookies] CookieJar scoping weaknesses (public suffix, IP hosts, Secure overwrite, prefixes, size caps)
body:
## Summary
The cookie jar deviates from RFC 6265/6265bis in several ways that allow cross-site cookie setting and overwrite.

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:23-90` — small hand-written public-suffix list
- `Runtime/Middleware/CookieJar.cs:354-359` — domain matching
- `GetCookieHeader` takes the write lock and scans all cookies on every request

## Problem
- Public suffixes like `github.io`, `blogspot.com`, `herokuapp.com`, `amazonaws.com`, `co.za`, `com.ua` are missing: a tenant can set `Domain=github.io` and affect all tenants.
- IP hosts not special-cased: `Domain=168.1.5` accepted for `192.168.1.5`.
- An http response can overwrite a `Secure` cookie (6265bis 'leave secure cookies alone').
- `__Host-`/`__Secure-` prefixes not enforced.
- No size caps on name/value/attributes (only count limits).
- Write lock per request serializes all requests.

## Spec reference
RFC 6265 §5.3, §5.1.3; draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis §4.1.3 (prefixes), §5.7 (leave secure cookies alone)

## Suggested fix
1. Ship a compact PSL (or allow plugging one) and reject domain cookies on suffixes.
2. IP-literal hosts: host-only cookies only, Domain must equal host.
3. Implement 'leave secure cookies alone', prefix rules, and 4096-byte name+value cap.
4. Use a reader/writer lock or copy-on-write snapshot for `GetCookieHeader`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Domain cookie on a public suffix is rejected
- [ ] Domain attribute on IP host is rejected unless equal to host
- [ ] Insecure response cannot overwrite a Secure cookie
- [ ] `__Host-`/`__Secure-` prefix tests
- [ ] Oversized cookies rejected

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Cache] In-memory variant index grows without bound
body:
## Summary
Every stored response registers a `VariantBucket`; buckets are only removed on lookup miss or invalidation, and storage eviction does not notify the interceptor.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:909` — `RegisterStoredVariant`
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:978` — bucket removal paths
- `MemoryCacheStorage` evicts silently (default 100 entries)

## Problem
An app fetching many unique URLs (thumbnails, signed URLs) leaks one bucket per URL for the lifetime of the interceptor.

## Suggested fix
Add an eviction callback to `ICacheStorage` (or have the interceptor bound the index with LRU matching storage capacity).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Variant index size bounded by storage capacity
- [ ] Test: store 10k unique URLs with capacity 100 -> index size <= 100 (+small slack)

title: [Cache] Response headers instance shared between consumer and background cache store
body:
## Summary
The same `HttpHeaders` instance is passed to the inner handler (exposed as `UHttpResponse.Headers`) and queued for background storage.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheStoringHandler.cs:68-110` — `capturedHeaders` passed to `_inner.OnResponseStartAsync` and to `QueueStoreResponse` (deferred via `Task.Yield`)

## Problem
`HttpHeaders` is a non-thread-safe Dictionary and is publicly mutable. A consumer calling `Set`/`Add` on response headers while the store thread calls `Clone()` throws InvalidOperationException or stores a corrupted entry.

## Suggested fix
Clone headers synchronously before queueing the store (`capturedHeaders.Clone()`), so the store owns its copy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Store path never shares a mutable headers instance with the consumer
- [ ] Stress test mutating response headers concurrently with storage

## Context

title: [Core] Pooled UHttpRequest has no lease generation (ABA on stale references)
body:
## Summary
`UHttpRequest` is pooled; `ThrowIfDisposed` only checks `_isLeased == 0 || _disposeRequested`, so a stale reference to a recycled request passes the check after it is re-leased.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs` — `ThrowIfDisposed`, `ResetForPool`, lease flags
- `SendBufferedAsync` auto-disposes the request

## Problem
User code keeps a reference (e.g. retry loop) and calls `req.WithHeader(...)` or `SendBufferedAsync()` after the request was returned and re-leased by another task; the mutation/send lands on someone else's request (wrong headers, credentials crossing requests).

## Suggested fix
Add a lease generation/token: builder methods capture the generation at lease time and throw `ObjectDisposedException` when it differs; or stop pooling the user-facing request object.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Using a request after it was returned to the pool always throws, even if re-leased
- [ ] Regression test: dispose, re-lease from another caller, mutate stale ref -> throws

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Core] UHttpClient disposes interceptors it does not own
body:
## Summary
`DisposeConfiguredInterceptors` disposes every `IDisposable` in `_options.Interceptors`; `UHttpClientOptions.Clone` shares instances.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:483` — `DisposeConfiguredInterceptors`

## Problem
One `CacheInterceptor`/`CookieInterceptor`/`ConcurrencyInterceptor` shared between two clients: disposing the first client makes the second throw `ObjectDisposedException` on every request.

## Suggested fix
Add explicit ownership (`UHttpClientOptions.DisposeInterceptors` / `ownsInterceptors`, default false for caller-supplied instances) or reference-count shared interceptors.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Disposing one client does not break another sharing an interceptor
- [ ] Ownership semantics documented and tested

body:
## Summary
`UHttpClientOptions.FollowRedirects = true` and `MaxRedirects = 10` are defaults, but nothing follows redirects unless the Middleware module's `RedirectInterceptor` is added manually.

title: [Observability] LoggingInterceptor logs full URLs (query tokens) and redacts too few headers
body:
## Summary
Logging writes the full request URI including query string, and the default sensitive-header list misses common credential headers.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/LoggingInterceptor.cs:86` — URL logged unredacted
- `Runtime/Observability/LoggingHandler.cs` — response logging
- Default redaction list: Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, WWW-Authenticate, X-Api-Key

## Problem
`?access_token=...`, OAuth `code=`, or pre-signed URLs (S3/GCS signatures) go into the log sink and device logs. Headers such as `X-Auth-Token`, `X-Amz-Security-Token`, `X-Goog-Api-Key`, `Api-Key`, `X-CSRF-Token`, `Proxy-Authenticate` are logged in clear.

## Suggested fix
1. Redact query values by default (keep names), with an opt-out.
2. Extend the default header list and make it configurable (add/remove).
3. Share one redaction policy with the Editor Monitor (see Unity/Editor issue).

title: [Files] FileDownloader resume is unsafe (no If-Range, partial at final path, unchecked Content-Range)
body:
## Summary
Resume logic can splice different representations together and cannot distinguish partial from complete files.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:111-125` — Range request built without `If-Range`
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:171-184` — 206 with missing/unparseable `Content-Range` appended (`rangeStart` -1 passes)
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:180` — partial written at the final path; checksum failure leaves corrupt file

## Problem
- Resource changed between attempts: new bytes appended to old partial file -> corrupt file (checksum optional).
- Truncated download looks identical to a finished one.
- 206 without Content-Range is trusted.
- Range requests don't force `Accept-Encoding: identity`; with Decompression in the chain, a compressed range fails to decode and progress total is 0.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §13.1.5 (If-Range), §14.4 (Content-Range), §15.3.7

## Suggested fix
1. Persist ETag/Last-Modified with the partial (sidecar) and send `If-Range`.
2. Write to `<path>.part`, rename on success.
3. Require a valid `Content-Range` whose start equals the existing size; otherwise restart.
4. Delete/quarantine on checksum failure.
5. Send `Accept-Encoding: identity` on Range requests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Changed resource restarts download instead of splicing
- [ ] Final path only exists after verified completion
- [ ] 206 without valid Content-Range restarts
- [ ] Tests for each case

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Auth] OAuth token parsing depends on reflection into TurboHTTP.JSON that IL2CPP can strip
body:
## Summary
`OAuthClient` reaches JSON through `ProjectJsonBridge` reflection; the reflected methods are not preserved and the Auth→JSON dependency is undeclared.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProjectJsonBridge.cs` — `Type.GetType("TurboHTTP.JSON.JsonSerializer, TurboHTTP.JSON")`, `GetMethod("Deserialize"/"Serialize")` with `(string, Type)` / `(object, Type)`
- `Runtime/JSON/link.xml` — preserves only `JsonExtensions`
- Auth has no link.xml

## Problem
At Medium/High managed stripping the two static overloads (no static callers) can be removed; OAuth token parsing then fails at runtime on device. If the JSON assembly is not referenced by the project at all, OAuth silently fails.

## Suggested fix
1. Preserve `JsonSerializer` and the reflected overloads (link.xml + `[Preserve]`), or
2. Give Auth a tiny internal token-response parser (flat JSON object) and drop the reflection dependency.
3. Fail with a clear error message if JSON is unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OAuth refresh works in an IL2CPP build with High stripping
- [ ] Clear error if the JSON module is missing
- [ ] Device validation recorded

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible (needs device/runtime confirmation).

title: [Cache] 304 merge overwrites representation metadata; Expires used without Date correction
body:
## Summary
Revalidation merge copies every 304 header over the stored response and freshness uses the device clock without correction.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs` — `MergeNotModifiedEntry`
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs` — `ResolveExpiry`

## Problem
- 304 carrying `Content-Length: 0`, `Content-Encoding` or `Content-Type` corrupts the stored 200's metadata (body later truncated or mis-decoded).
- Stale stored `Age` survives the merge, shortening freshness.
- `Expires` evaluated against the device clock; mobile clock skew makes entries never fresh or fresh for hours.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 §3.2 (updating stored headers), §4.2.1–4.2.3 (freshness, age calculation)

## Suggested fix
1. Exclude `Content-Length`, `Content-Encoding`, `Content-Range`, `Transfer-Encoding` (and hop-by-hop headers) from the merge; drop old `Age`.
2. Compute freshness per RFC 9111 §4.2 using `Date` (apparent_age/corrected age) and `Expires - Date`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 304 merge never changes body-framing headers
- [ ] Freshness correct with skewed device clock (unit test with injected clock)

## Context

title: [Auth] OAuth refresh deadlocks when OAuthClient uses a client that carries the OAuth AuthInterceptor

title: [Cache] SegmentedBuffer leak and undisposed CTS when CacheInterceptor is disposed
body:
## Summary
Queued background store mutations return early on cancellation before the `try/finally` that disposes the body.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:489` and `:865` — early `return`/`ThrowIfCancellationRequested` before body disposal
- `_backgroundWorkCancellation` never disposed

## Problem
After `CacheInterceptor.Dispose`, pending stores leak pooled `SegmentedBuffer` segments (ArrayPool pressure) and the CTS.

## Suggested fix
Move the cancellation check inside the `try` (or dispose the body in every early-exit path); dispose `_backgroundWorkCancellation` in `Dispose`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pool counters return to baseline after dispose with pending stores
- [ ] Leak test using pool diagnostics

title: [Cache] Cache key normalization aliases distinct URLs
body:
## Summary
Cache key normalization drops empty path segments and sorts query parameters.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.UriNormalization.cs` — `NormalizePath`, `NormalizeQuery`

## Problem
`/a//b` and `/a/b`, or `?b=1&a=2` and `?a=2&b=1`, share one cache entry. Order-sensitive servers and signed URLs (signature over ordered query) can receive the wrong cached response.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 §2 (cache key = target URI), RFC 3986 §6.2.2

## Suggested fix
Key on the URI as sent (scheme/host lower-cased, default port removed, percent-encoding normalized per RFC 3986 §6.2.2 only). Make aggressive normalization opt-in.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Distinct paths/query orders produce distinct keys by default
- [ ] Tests

title: [RateLimit] ConcurrencyLimiter host-semaphore eviction race
body:
## Summary
Idle per-host semaphores are evicted while waiters may still hold references; a new semaphore is created for the same host.

## Location
- `Runtime/RateLimit/ConcurrencyLimiter.cs:197-231` — eviction above 1024 hosts

## Problem
Above 1024 hosts: limit for a host doubles (old + new semaphore); `Release(host)` releases the new one, which was created with `maxCount == initial` -> `SemaphoreFullException` from the interceptor's `finally`. Also unverified: whether the permit is held until the end of a streamed body or released when headers arrive.

## Suggested fix
Reference-count host entries (evict only when count is 0 under lock), and have `Release` use the semaphore instance captured at acquire. Verify/document permit lifetime for streaming responses.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No SemaphoreFullException under host churn stress test
- [ ] Per-host limit never exceeded
- [ ] Permit lifetime for streaming documented and tested

Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible (needs device/runtime confirmation).

title: [Middleware] Decompression default limit (256 MB) and buffered ToArray copy risk OOM on mobile
body:
## Summary
Default `DefaultMaxDecompressedBodySizeBytes` is 256 MB and the buffered path uses `MemoryStream` + `ToArray()` (~2x peak).

## Location
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionInterceptor.cs:17` — default limit
- `Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs` — buffered path

## Problem
A compression bomb or large legitimate response can allocate ~512 MB peak on a mobile device before the limit triggers.

## Suggested fix
Lower the default (e.g. 32 MB, configurable), decode into pooled segmented buffers instead of MemoryStream+ToArray.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Lower documented default
- [ ] Buffered decompression peak allocation ~1x body size (allocation test)

title: [JSON] LiteJson default serializer limitations (no POCOs, BOM, DateTime, lax parsing, no size limit)
body:
## Summary
The default `LiteJsonSerializer` fails common usage and is lax in parsing.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/*` — `LiteJsonSerializer`, `JsonReader`

## Problem
- Cannot deserialize into POCOs: `AsJson<T>`, `GetJsonAsync<T>`, `PostJsonAsync` fail at runtime for user types out of the box.
- UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) breaks parsing.
- `DateTime.Parse` without `RoundtripKind` shifts `Z` timestamps to local time.
- Accepts `1.`, unescaped control chars, Unicode whitespace (non RFC 8259).
- No input size limit (depth limit 64 is fine).
- Large decimals lose precision (long/ulong/double).

## Spec reference
RFC 8259

## Suggested fix
1. Either support POCO mapping (AOT-safe, e.g. generated/registered contracts) or fail at compile-time/with a clear message pointing to the System.Text.Json/Newtonsoft adapter; document prominently.
2. Skip BOM; use `DateTimeStyles.RoundtripKind`; strict RFC 8259 number/string grammar; configurable max input size; decimal option.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `AsJson<T>` for a POCO either works or throws a documented, actionable error
- [ ] BOM, `Z` timestamp and strict-grammar tests
- [ ] Input size limit test

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Core] InternalsVisibleTo boundary breach; no public safe-copy primitive for third-party interceptors
body:
## Summary
Core grants `InternalsVisibleTo` to 10 modules, which then depend on internals, while third-party interceptors lack the primitives first-party ones use.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/AssemblyInfo.cs` — IVT to Auth, Cache, Files, JSON, Middleware, Observability, Retry, Testing, Transport, WebSocket
- Cache uses `Core.Internal.SegmentedBuffer`, `BufferedResponseBodySource`; Middleware/Retry use `ResponseBodyDiscardHelper`; several use `UHttpRequest.CopyWithSharedContent`/`CreateDerived`
- Public `UHttpRequest.Clone()` throws for `StreamRequestBody`

## Problem
Optional modules cannot ship/version independently of Core (any internal change breaks them), and third-party interceptors cannot safely derive requests (e.g. for retries/redirects) or discard bodies the way first-party modules do — plug-and-play promise is weaker than advertised.

## Suggested fix
Promote the needed primitives to a small, documented public extension API (`IRequestDerivation`/`UHttpRequest.CreateDerived`, `ResponseBody.DiscardAsync`, pooled buffer access), then shrink IVT to Transport/Testing only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Public API covers request derivation and body discard
- [ ] IVT list reduced; modules compile without internals (except Transport/Testing)
- [ ] Sample third-party interceptor implementing retry with the public API

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (code path traced).

title: [Core] Reduce Core surface: move feature types out and hide internal pools
body:
## Summary
Core carries feature-specific types and exposes internals publicly, against the 'Core extraction' goal.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core` — `AdaptiveInterceptor`, `BackgroundNetworkingInterceptor`, `NetworkQualityDetector`, `ProxySettings`
- `Runtime/Core/Internal` — `ObjectPool<T>`, `ByteArrayPool` are `public`
- `Runtime/Core/ProjectJsonBridge.cs` — public

## Problem
Larger mandatory footprint for every user, public API surface that must be versioned/supported, and hidden coupling (ProjectJsonBridge reflection).

## Suggested fix
Move adaptive/background/network-quality into an optional module (e.g. TurboHTTP.Mobile/Adaptive); make pool types internal (expose via IVT to Transport only); make `ProjectJsonBridge` internal or replace with an explicit registration API. `ProxySettings` may stay if transport config requires it — document why.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Core public API listing reviewed and reduced
- [ ] Moved types live in optional modules with no Core->module references
- [ ] Breaking changes recorded in CHANGELOG
